surprising_finding: A flat's own old rent beats everything else, even when it is stale. The typical own rent we used was about 20 months old, yet once indexed it missed by about $41 on Fold A, against $100 for a recent suburb, bedrooms and parking median. The second surprise was in the supplied input: its parking and bedrooms track each flat's latest advert, so a simple date split quietly shows a model the answer. We rebuilt those fields as known at each cutoff.
what_worked: Indexing each flat's own last rent to the target date. This took the Fold A anchor bias from -$50 to +$3.62.
Rolling two-month training windows, so each training row faces the same gap as the real task.
Rebuilding parking and bedrooms as known at each cutoff. This removed a hidden leak and created 85 Fold B adverts that test the parking premium directly.

Noticing how landlords behave. About a quarter of re-lets within two years return at exactly the old rent, which an index cannot show. Adding the raw last rent improved Fold B by about $2 and flats with history most of all, while Fold A barely moved.
Blending. A nine-model blend reached $38.02 on Fold A before rounding, against $40.25 for LightGBM alone. Weights were chosen on earlier windows, and Fold A was read once for this blend.
what_didnt: Projecting the rent trend forward. Tuning on Fold B chose to hold the index flat at the cutoff.
Separating the two model targets. Log(rent / anchor) beat rent by about $1 on Fold B, and the winner changed when we removed features, so treat that choice as close to noise.

Public data. Thirteen sets of open-data features (G-NAF, OpenStreetMap, Census, cadastre, transport and amenities) gave no gain overall on Fold B. The best set helped first-time flats by perhaps $1 to $2 but cost flats with history about $1, and its first result did not repeat on fresh seeds.

Microburbs API data. Extra adverts, transport, schools, amenities, risks, noise and market series all missed our bar of $1 with a clear interval on Fold B. Market series came closest, at -$0.66. Crime was left out because its inputs are undated. Sale history was only 26% pulled, so it is untested.

Using the model's own parking gap. It came out around $17 to $22, compressed because anchors stay fixed between passes. We use the within-building premium, median $36. The two could not be separated on 85 Fold B adverts whose parking changed.
Model tuning. Hyperparameters, CatBoost, blends and separate models for first-time flats all stayed within noise.
Any single bigger model. TabPFN, TabICL, TabM and RealMLP gave no reliable win over plain trees on all rows. The gain came from blending many different models instead.

journey.change: Median rent for the same suburb, bedrooms and parking over the last 12 months. The tidy $100 is real: most adverts and medians sit on round numbers, so 190 of 2,635 errors are exactly $100, and the median lands on one of them.
Use the flat's own last advert, or its building's, instead of a local median. Stale, so it ran $50 low.
Bring that old rent up to date using how repeat leases of the same flats moved.
We found the input was showing us each test advert's own parking and bedrooms, and removed that. The Fold A score got slightly worse, and the result became believable.
Learn how far to trust each anchor, using rolling two-month training windows.
Drop date fields that looked nothing like the flats we predict, and predict the ratio to the anchor.
Show the model the flat's last rent as advertised, because many re-lets return at exactly the old rent. Add 5-seed averaging. Fold B improved by about $2, Fold A barely moved.
Blend nine tree, linear, neighbour and neural models, with weights chosen only on earlier windows, and add more flat-history features.
Quote rents in $10 steps, the way adverts are written. The median error rose to $40, but more adverts landed within $100 and bias fell to zero. This is the submitted file.

limitations: Rounding to $10 means errors fall on $10 steps, so the median can jump in steps on the real adverts. Fold B's blend weights also saw Fold B, so its $39.87 is not a clean test.
